ABSTRACT 49

OBJECTIVE 50

Acromegaly is a rare neuroendocrine condition that can lead to significant morbidity; therefore, 51

large studies are invaluable for understanding the disease burden. Despite China’s vast 52

population size, studies on acromegaly remain sparse. In this report, we aimed to investigate 53

clinical characteristics and predictors of biochemical remission after surgery for acromegaly. 54

METHODS 55

A retrospective nationwide study was conducted using patient-reported data from the China 56

Acromegaly Patient Association (CAPA) from 1998 to 2018. Univariate analyses were 57

performed using Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, two-sample t-tests, and chi-squared tests. Using the 58

purposeful selection method, multivariate logistic regression analysis was employed to determine 59

independent predictors of biochemical remission at 3 months in patients after surgery. 60

RESULTS: Of the 575 cases (mean age: 37.3 years; 59% female), macroadenomas and invasive 61

tumors (Knosp score 3-4) were 87% and 61%, respectively. Ninety-five percent of patients were 62

treated first with surgery (5.1% transcranial and 94.9% endonasal) and 38.3% exhibited 63

biochemical remission at 3-months postoperatively. The following independent predictors of 64

biochemical remission were identified: preoperative growth hormone (GH) levels between 12 65

and 28 μg/L [odds ratio (OR)=0.61; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.39-0.96; p=0.031], 66

preoperative GH levels >28 μg/L (OR=0.56; 95% CI, 0.35-0.90; p=0.016), macroadenoma 67

(OR=0.57; 95% CI, 0.33-0.97; p=0.041), giant adenomas (OR=0.17; 95% CI, 0.06-0.44; 68

p=0.0005), Knosp score 3-4 (OR=0.39; 95% CI, 0.25-0.59; p<0.0001), and preoperative 69

medication usage (OR=2.16; 95% CI, 1.38-3.39; p=0.0008). 70

CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide study spanning over two decades, we highlight that higher 71

preoperative GH levels, large tumor size, and greater extent of tumor invasiveness are associated 72

with a lower likelihood of biochemical remission at 3-months after surgery, while preoperative 73

medical therapy increases the chance of remission. 74

Introduction 102

Acromegaly is a rare condition characterized by the overproduction of growth hormone 103

(GH) from a hypersecreting pituitary tumor.1–3 Clinical manifestations of GH-secreting tumors 104

can manifest insidiously and result in a delayed diagnosis, while the systemic repercussions of 105

insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) excess, resultant from GH stimulation, are associated with 106

increased morbidity and mortality.4 Symptoms and signs of acromegaly include facial changes, 107

excessive skeletal growth, soft tissue hypertrophy, obstructive sleep apnea, hyperhidrosis, 108

headache, and visual impairments.2,5–7 Persistent high levels of GH and/or IGF-1 may also result 109

in glucose intolerance, osteoporosis, arthritis, reproductive disorders, and cardiovascular 110

dysfunction, ultimately driving premature mortality.2,4–7 111

Given the rarity of acromegaly, large studies that characterize the disease 112

pattern, describe risk factors predictive of poor disease control and inform management decisions 113

of this condition are scarce. In particular, there is a notable gap in data regarding prevalence, 114

disease severity, treatments administered, and clinical outcomes for acromegaly patients in China. 115

We present the first report from the China Acromegaly Patient Association (CAPA), which is a 116

Methods 123

124

Study Design and Data Collection 125

126

We retrospectively reviewed the records of 916 acromegaly patients enrolled into the 127

multi-institutional China Acromegaly Patient Association (CAPA) database 128

(https://capa.wohenok.com) between June 1998 and December 2018. The CAPA database is 129

patient-reported and relies on the patient submission of demographic and clinical information 130

following the diagnosis and treatment of acromegaly, drawing upon patient information from 131

112 hospitals across China (Supplemental Materials S1). Patients lacking data on treatment 132

interventions or biochemical status at follow-up were excluded from the analysis, resulting in a 133

final cohort of 575 patients. 134

We extracted demographic data (including age, sex, location of residence, and insurance 135

type), disease duration, clinical symptoms, biochemical status (at diagnosis and on follow-up), 136

radiographic features, treatment history, histopathology, postoperative complications, and 137

follow-up at 3 months after treatment. Approval (approved ID [2020] 091) for this retrospective 138

Variables Analyzed 142

143

All patients in the CAPA database were diagnosed with acromegaly in accordance with 144

Location of residence 157

The geographic grouping was performed based on the Yicai Media Group 158

(https://www.yicai.com) stratification of Chinese cities and towns into 5 tiers, which we adapted 159

to classify patient residence into the following categories based on population density and size of 160

economy: large city, medium city, and small city/town. 161

162

Insurance coverage 163

There are three insurance schemes in China, including the urban employee-based basic 164

medical insurance scheme (UEBMI; launched in 1998), urban resident-based basic medical 165

insurance scheme (URBMI; launched in 2007), and rural new cooperative medical scheme 166

(NCMS; launched in 2003), which is intended to provide affordable health insurance for the poor 167

and improve the equity of health services in rural China.12 In general, UEBMI covers a broader 168

array of medical services than URBMI, with NCMS having the least robust coverage. 169

Treatment 170

171

Primary treatment modalities included medication, radiotherapy, or surgery, which 172

comprised of microscopic endonasal, endoscopic endonasal, or transcranial surgery (Figure 1). 173

Outcome Measures 181

182

The primary outcome of interest was biochemical remission at 3 months postoperatively. 183

The recurrence rate was also identified using the latest follow up information. The criteria for 184

postoperative biochemical remission after surgery for acromegaly were based on the established 185

guidelines (Box 1).8 186

Statistical Analysis 188

189

Baseline characteristics were described using mean ± standard deviation (SD), median 190

(interquartile range, IQR), or frequency according to the variable type. Group differences were 191

compared using the two-sample Student’s t-test or Mann-Whitney U-test for continuous 192

variables, and Pearson’s chi-squared test (two-tailed) or Fisher’s exact test for categorical 193

variables, as appropriate. The family discovery rate (FDR) correction was performed across all 194

univariate analyses to adjust for multiple testing. A purposeful selection approach to multivariate 195

logistic regression analysis was performed to determine the independent predictors of 196

Results 203

Cohort 204

205

We retrospectively analyzed presenting features, imaging, and clinical outcomes for 575 206

acromegaly patients (mean age 37.3±10.3 years; 59% women) from the multi-institutional 207

patient-reported CAPA database. The median time from symptom onset to diagnosis was 5 years 208

(range: 1-10 years). The most common clinical symptoms and signs at presentation were 209

enlarged nose and prognathism (97.4%) (Table 1). Visual field abnormalities, resulting from 210

tumor mass effect, occurred in 49.2% of patients.  Apoplexy occurred in 9.6%, producing tumor 211

mass effect. Other comorbidities associated with acromegaly were reported as follows: 212

cardiovascular disease (40.0%), impaired glucose tolerance (31.0%), osteoporosis (22.6%), 213

colonic polyps (16.3%), arthritis (15.8%), and colon cancer (0.7%). 214

Large and giant tumors dominated this cohort, with 73.2% being macroadenomas, 10.1% 215

being giant adenomas, and 16.7% being microadenomas (Table 2, Figure 2A). Consistent with 216

the prevalence of large tumors in this cohort, two-thirds of the tumors demonstrated cavernous 217

sinus invasion (Table 2, Figure 2A). 218

Endocrinological Status 227

228

Among 575 acromegaly patients, the mean levels of GH and IGF-1 prior to surgery were 229

26.8 μg/L and 781.5 μg/L respectively. Mean preoperative GH level was significantly higher in 230

patients with macroadenomas (27.3 μg/L) and giant adenomas (36.8 μg/L) compared to those 231

with microadenomas (18.5 μg/L) (both p<0.001) (Figure 2B). Additionally, tumors with 232

cavernous sinus invasion exhibited significantly higher median GH levels than those without 233

invasion (28.7 μg/L vs. 23.3 μg/L, p<0.001) (Figure 2C). Tumors with plurihormonal expression 234

showed higher median GH levels (22.7 μg/L) than dual-staining pituitary tumors of GH and 235

prolactin (DSPTs) (20.0 μg/L) and GH alone (16.5 μg/L), but these differences did not reach a 236

statistical significance. 237

Surgical Outcome 250

251

Among the 546 patients who underwent initial surgical resection, histopathology 252

confirmed immunopositivity for GH alone in 81.5%, concurrent GH and prolactin staining in 253

13.7%, and the presence of additional hormone expression along with GH in the remaining 254

(4.8%) (Table 2). Tumors that stained for both GH and prolactin were more likely than solely 255

GH-staining tumors to be invasive (78.7% vs. 61.1%, respectively; p=0.003).14 Moreover, the 256

most common postoperative complication was postoperative hyponatremia (sodium <135 257

mmol/L) (26.0%), followed by diabetes insipidus (18.5%), cerebrospinal fluid leak (6.8%), 258

meningitis (0.4%). One case of internal carotid artery (ICA) injury was reported. 259

At three months after surgery, 209 (38.3%) patients had achieved biochemical remission 260

(Table 3, Figure 1). More aggressive tumors were associated with a lower likelihood of 261

remission at 3 months. Specifically, higher pre-operative GH levels, larger tumors, and the 262

presence of cavernous sinus invasion were all significantly associated with lack of remission 263

Discussion 289

We present the clinical characteristics of over 500 acromegaly patients in China and 290

observe tumor and treatment factors strongly associated with disease control at three months 291

after surgery or other definitive treatment. Our study represents the largest analysis of clinical 292

features and postoperative outcomes of acromegaly in China, and also constitutes the first 293

application of the CAPA database for clinical research. We observed a 3-month postoperative 294

remission rate of 38.3%, with the likelihood of disease control strongly influenced by the 295

preoperative GH level, tumor size, and tumor invasiveness as indicated by the Knosp grade. 296

Despite China’s vast population size, medical studies on acromegaly remain sparse, 297

particularly in English-language journals. The earliest record of a surgical case of acromegaly in 298

China dates back to 1929, when the first patient was operated on using transcranial surgery at the 299

Peking Union Medical College Hospital (records endure in archives of the hospital library). 300

Early published studies from China were mostly case series and smaller cohorts. More recently, a 301

single-institution retrospective analysis of 358 Chinese acromegalic patients found the GH 302

remission rate to be 37.3% in patients with invasive macroadenomas without receipt of 303

preoperative somatostatin analogs as compared to 56.4% among those with pre-operative 304

medical treatment.15 We drew upon the power of a patient-reported database to expand on the 305

clinical experience in the diagnosis and treatment of acromegaly in China across multiple 306

institutions. 307

Clinical characteristics 309

310

Although the most commonly reported physical changes in our cohort were similar to 311

previously published series,2,16 the detection of such changes may occur in a delayed fashion 312

given the typically insidious onset over decades. Additionally, dental malocclusion, median 313

thenar neuropathy (carpal tunnel syndrome), change in shoe size or ring size, and skin tags may 314

be overlooked signs of acromegaly. Sleep apnea, headache, and hyperhidrosis were observed in 315

over half of patients, in addition to menstrual disturbances in two-thirds of female patients. 316

These, among other common non-physical, symptoms should prompt closer inspection for 317

physical signs of acromegaly and consideration for endocrinological evaluation, including 318

assaying IGF-1 determinations. 319

Although visual field deficit clearly triggers an alarm for a compressive etiology 320

involving the optic apparatus, 52.5% of patients with macroadenomas did not report any 321

subjective visual impairment. Clinical concern for a large pituitary tumor, as in aggressive 322

acromegaly cases, should prompt formal neuro-ophthalmologic evaluation. 323

Acromegaly is associated with premature mortality.17,18 Older age at diagnosis, increased 324

time from symptom onset to diagnosis, higher GH levels after treatment, and cardiovascular risk 325

factors are independent predictors of early mortality.18 Forty percent of patients in this cohort 326

reported cardiovascular symptoms or disease, including heart palpitations, arrhythmias (e.g., 327

atrial fibrillation and heart block), structural heart diseases (e.g., cardiomyopathy and valvular 328

disease), and hypertension. These findings, when viewed in light of the fact that the mean age of 329

our cohort was only 37.3 years, underscores the strikingly significant impact of acromegaly on 330

cardiovascular health.19 Furthermore, the high incidence of impaired glucose tolerance (diabetes 331

Factors influencing biochemical remission 338

339

The 38.3% biochemical remission rate at 3-months after surgery for a GH secreting 340

tumor in our cohort is relatively low compared to other reports in the literature.20,21 This may 341

reflect the high proportion of large and invasive tumors encompassed by our cohort. Additionally, 342

cultural factors and health literacy for neuroendocrinological diseases may contribute to a delay 343

in seeking medical care, resulting in the disease progression. In addition, 1 in 5 patients in our 344

cohort was from a small city or town, which may further delay access to medical care and 345

endocrinological evaluation. Although we did not observe a statistically significant impact of 346

socioeconomic or insurance status on the likelihood of biochemical remission after surgery for 347

acromegaly in this patient-reported cohort, further investigations are merited to improve the 348

delay between diagnosis and treatment, and also potential delays in the initial recognition of 349

acromegaly, especially amongst individuals with geographical and financial barriers. 350

Preoperative clinical and biochemical characteristics could impact the likelihood of 351

biochemical remission, including age at diagnosis,22 gender,22 preoperative serum levels of GH 352

and IGF-1,20,23–27 tumor size,20,24,28,29 preoperative medication usage,15,21 tumor 353

invasiveness,20,24,27–31 and histological pathology.24,30 Similar to other studies, our analysis also 354

revealed that larger tumors (giant and macroadenomas) were less likely than small tumors to 355

enter biochemical remission at 3 months. Further, patients with invasive tumors and higher 356

preoperative GH levels were less likely to attain remission, adjusted for tumor size and receipt of 357

preoperative medical therapy. Given that aggressive tumors were shown to be less likely to enter 358

biochemical remission postoperatively, early surgical intervention should be instituted to halt 359

further progression of disease.32 360

Pharmaceutical treatment, including somatostatin receptor ligands (SRLs), growth 361

hormone receptor antagonists, and dopamine agonists (DA), have shown to have a beneficial 362

impact on surgical outcomes as both neoadjuvant and adjuvant therapy,15,21 which was also 363

demonstrated by our team.33 In particular, administration of somatostatin analogs prior to surgery 364

is associated with higher endocrinological remission than adjuvant treatment alone.15,34–37 365

Likewise, the use of preoperative medical treatment more than doubled the odds of remission in 366

our cohort. 367

Long-term remission in patients with initial remission showed a delayed improvement of 368

biochemical remission. Among secondary treatments in patients without initial remission, the 369

lowest recurrence rate presented in patients undergoing repeat surgery, the necessity of which is 370

highlighted in persistent cases with invasive tumors.38,39 371

372

Limitations 373

Our study strengthens the insight into the patterns of care and results of treatment for 374

acromegaly in China. The vast heterogeneity in the regional economy, insurance coverage, 375

education, health literacy, and accessibility of medical care, however, may limit the 376

generalizability of these results to all acromegaly patients in China. The self-reported nature of 377

resection, detailed pathological results (Ki-67, somatostatin receptor subtype 2 expression, AIP 379

expression, and granularity), dates of secondary treatment, and continuous follow-ups. Although 380

we have the last follow-up record, which might underestimate the time to recurrence and 381

therefore limit us to further investigate predictors of long-term outcomes. Finally, as evidenced 382

by the low median age of our cohort, the majority of patients who contributed to this database 383

through online submission were young, likely reflecting age-related biases in adopting an 384

electronic reporting platform. Strategies to expand access and ease of data accrual from more 385

diverse populations, both in demographics and age, may further diversify the value of this 386

clinical database in the future. 387

388

Conclusions 389

We present the largest nation-wide analysis of clinical features and surgical outcomes of 390

acromegaly patients in China, driven from a patient-reported database. We highlight that higher 391

preoperative GH levels, giant adenomas, and greater extent of tumor invasiveness are associated 392

with a lower likelihood of biochemical remission at 3-months after surgery, while preoperative 393

medical therapy increases the chance of remission. Importantly, we have established the 394

effectiveness and potential of a patient-reported database in advancing neuroendocrinological 395

research. 396
